description:
MEDIUM AND MATERIAL. Twelve centred radial rosettes on a near-black charcoal ground. The whole work is built from essentially one primitive, the annulus: thick flat gold donuts, thinner outlined circles, and tiny ring-dots, repeated around a shared centre at roughly six- to eight-fold rotational symmetry and stacked in translucent layers so that overlaps darken into moire. Only two hues are ever used, an ochre/mustard gold and a dusty slate blue-grey, both desaturated, sitting on charcoal. Some fills are crisp flat vector; others (the large blue central discs, the gold under-mass) are soft-edged and blurred, and in the 512 view the gold under-mass carries dark brushed striations like scratched or smeared paint under the clean rings.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. Nothing literal. The nearest referents are a lace doily, a spirograph drawing, a mandala or rose window, and a sectioned flower head or sea-urchin test. Every token is a single bounded object floating at the centre of an empty black field: an emblem, a medallion, a specimen photographed against black.

WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE. Identical structural grammar in all twelve: one centred mass, strict radial symmetry, a scalloped circular silhouette made of overlapping ring lobes, a distinct inner core (usually a large blue disc or a gold disc with fine gold filigree on it) and an outer wreath of larger rings. Same two colours, same ground, same centring, same scale-of-detail progression from large outer rings to tiny central ones. There is no seed that breaks the format.

HOW THEY DIFFER. The axes of variation are density, overall scale, ring size, and the gold/blue ratio -- not shape. 1733538 is the outlier: a small pale gold blob with a scatter of tiny ring-dots around it and a great deal of black left visible; it is by far the emptiest and quietest. 1985692 and 1310661 are at the other end, so large and dense that they run off the left and right edges of their cells. 1475115 and 1561509 invert the usual colour hierarchy -- blue rings dominate the mass and gold is pushed into the core -- and are the only two that read blue at a glance. 1243682 is the only one with real asymmetry of placement: loose gold donuts drift out to the upper left, lower left and lower right, off the main body, breaking the otherwise perfect containment. 1446330 is airy and open, a ring of blue circles with black showing between them and small gold dots outside. 1283437 is small, tidy and legible: a scalloped gold wreath, a big soft blue disc, a neat gold ring-rosette at the centre. 1203347, 1366079, 1835793 and 1991107 are the middle of the distribution and are the four that most resemble each other -- gold wreath, blue disc or blue band, gold filigree core.

ACROSS THE THREE MARKET STATES (seen on 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1310661). The change is real and visible, and its dominant direction is GROWTH AND BRIGHTENING, not damage. Neutral is the smallest, darkest and most contained state, with the most black ground around the object. Stress makes every seed noticeably LARGER, paler and more crowded: 1203347 stress swells until it clips all four edges of its cell and its scalloped silhouette is squared off by the frame; 1283437 stress grows from a modest wreath into a much fuller disc with an enlarged blue centre; 1310661 stress fills its cell edge to edge and the black ground almost disappears. Recovery is roughly the same size as stress but reorganises the blue: 1283437 recovery multiplies the little gold rings across the blue disc and opens the outer wreath into distinct scalloped lobes; 1243682 recovery breaks the blue petals into many smaller rings; 1310661 recovery thickens the blue lattice into rounder, heavier loops. The exception, and it is a large one, is 1203347 recovery, where the blue almost entirely leaves the work -- all that survives is a few faint blue crescent arcs on a flat gold field -- so that token changes colour identity between states rather than changing its structure.

WHAT SURVIVES AT 120px. The format survives completely and the individual tokens survive only partially. At browse size every cell is legibly a gold-and-blue radial rosette on black, and the three or four extremes stay tellable apart: 1733538 (nearly empty), 1310661 (big and dense), 1561509 and 1475115 (blue-dominant), 1243682 (satellites drifting off the body). The other seven converge: 1203347, 1366079, 1835793, 1991107, 1985692 and 1283437 all reduce to the same gold scalloped disc with a blue middle, separable only by fine density differences that are exactly the thing 120px destroys. Silhouette does no work here at all -- every token is the same circle -- so all the identity is carried by internal texture, which is the first casualty of the size. The state rows do survive at 120: neutral reads visibly smaller and darker than stress in all four seeds. But 1203347 stress and 1310661 stress at 120 read as flat gold squares, the outline lost to clipping, and 1310661 stress is close to undifferentiated mush.
